Question: If \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are in geometric progression (G.P.) with \(1\lt a\lt b\lt c\) and \(n\gt1\) is an integer, then \(\log_a n,\) \(\log_b n,\) \(\log_c n\) form a sequence

Choices.C:
in which the reciprocals of the terms form an
A.P.
Choices.D:
in which the second and third terms are the \(n\)th powers of
the first and second respectively

Solution:
A change of logarithm base makes the reciprocals easier to compare. Since \(a,b,c,n>1\), all the given logarithms are defined and positive, so their reciprocals exist. The change-of-base formula gives
\[
\frac1{\log_a n}=\log_n a,
\qquad
\frac1{\log_b n}=\log_n b,
\qquad
\frac1{\log_c n}=\log_n c.
\]
Because \(a,b,c\) are in geometric progression,
\[
\frac ba=\frac cb,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad b^2=ac.
\]
Taking logarithms to the valid base \(n>1\) yields
\[
2\log_n b=\log_n a+\log_n c.
\]
Thus the middle reciprocal is the arithmetic mean of the two outer reciprocals. Equivalently, their adjacent differences are equal, so the reciprocals form an arithmetic progression. The answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
